To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the similarity of multiunit activity to repeated sequences of AAB tone triplets is highest when A and B tones have the same phase spectrum, and that this similarity is correlated with the perceptual grouping of A and B tones into a single auditory perceptual stream.

the similarity of multiunit activity in monkey primary auditory cortex for tone sequences that are similar or dissimilar perceptually is correlated with the similarity of the phase spectrum of the tone sequences.

the similarity of the neuronal response to the A and B tone triplets was highest with the A tones having cosine phase and the alternating-phase B tones having cosine phase; it was lowest when the B tones were composed by adding the harmonies with random phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain processes the auditory world.
understanding the neuronal mechanisms of auditory scene analysis.
the neuronal mechanisms of auditory streaming, which is a perceptual phenomenon of grouping together similar sounds and segregating them from dissimilar sounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the primary auditory cortex is involved in the segregation of auditory objects.
auditory streaming in monkeys is a cortical process.
the neuronal correlates of auditory streaming in the primary and nonprimary auditory cortices are similar, and that these correlates reflect a separation of auditory streams in the cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neuronal activity in the primate primary auditory cortex can reflect auditory streaming of sound sequence, and this activity can be used to predict the perceptual outcome of auditory streaming.
the similarity of the neuronal response to a tone triplet is a good predictor of perceptual similarity for the triplet.
the similarity in neuronal activity in monkey auditory cortex correlates with the similarity in perceptual experience in human auditory streaming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neuronal correlate of auditory streaming is not a simple reflection of the similarity of neuronal activity in response to the different tone complexes.
neuronal activity in the auditory cortex is a correlate of auditory percept, and the activity can be measured by microelectrode recording.
neuronal activity in the monkey’s primary auditory cortex is correlated with the auditory perceptual streaming of sound sequences.
